transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Hassan, thanks for coming in to see me today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope this is a quick one. I've got a lot going on and my back is killing me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Look, I wanted to talk to you and your wife about the delivery last week. There were some things that didn't go quite right with the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean? Didn't go right how?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion regarding the prenatal records. Some information didn't make it over to the labor and delivery team in time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion. That's a vague word. I've heard that word from you people before when something actually went wrong. What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a system issue, really. The documentation just wasn't flagged properly for the nurses during the birth.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the system. I care about my daughter. Is she okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable, but she is being monitored very closely.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why is she being monitored if everything was fine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, some of the prophylactic measures weren't administered. It's a complicated coordination of care between the prenatal clinic and the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're dodging the question. Did you guys miss something?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're feeling really frustrated and worn out by this. I know you've had a lot of bad experiences here in the past.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not frustrated. I'm exhausted. I'm tired of being the one who has to double-check everything because you lot can't read a chart.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a lot to deal with. I really do recognize how heavy this feels for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So just tell me. What was missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some gaps in the communication flow. We're looking into how the records were handled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not asking for a corporate audit. I'm asking what my daughter was missing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the records didn't trigger the necessary alerts for the staff.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're still not saying it. Did she miss an antibiotic?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the timing of certain medications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My god, you can't even just say the words. Is she at risk for an infection because someone didn't check a box?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell this is incredibly stressful for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop telling me how I feel and tell me what you did. Or didn't do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a breakdown in the hand-off between departments.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a systemic failure. The software didn't alert the team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't give a damn about the software. Was it your job to check?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check on another patient in a moment, but we are managing her care now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? You're just going to leave me with "systemic failure" and "confusion" and then walk out?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure we are on the same page about her being stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We aren't on the same page because you haven't told me the truth. You're talking in circles.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm trying to be as clear as I can.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're being slippery. This is exactly what happened with my pain management last year. You hide behind "process" until the patient almost dies.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling cynical about the way we do things here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not feeling cynical. I am cynical. There is a difference. Now, what is the plan to fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep monitoring her and we'll see how her labs look tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What labs? Which ones?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just the standard newborn screens. We'll stay tuned to those.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. That's just waiting. What happens if the labs are bad?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll address it if it comes up. You might get an email from the portal with the results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I shouldn't be checking a portal for my newborn's infection risk. I want a timeline.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We're just taking it day by day.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's what you said three times during my last admission before they found the bleed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do understand why you're worried.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop. Just stop. Who is the person in charge of this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The attending is overseeing the case.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak with them.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can put in a request, but as I said, I really need to wrap this up and get to my other patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Unbelievable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll touch base again soon.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to go check on another patient', 'I really need to wrap this up') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: Resident never explicitly names the error, relying entirely on platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'confusion' despite direct patient questioning.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is consistently deflected to 'systemic failure' and 'the software'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrated', 'worn out', 'cynical') and attempts to engage with the patient's distress.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('we'll see', 'stay tuned', 'taking it day by day') with no concrete timeline or patient role.
